tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

schema.name: ScheduleWakeup
schema.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	# Issue #230: a web control surface on the remote port. Investigation notes
2	
3	Worktree: `/Users/sbgragent/.dispatch/worktrees/340ccb28`, branch `dispatch/230-a-web-control-surface-the-remote-port-se`, base `7fe8949` (Release 0.4.1). Read-only investigation: no code, tests or builds were run, and no browser was used.
4	
5	Sources read: `CLAUDE.md` (given in context), `docs/remote-client.md` (lines 1–396 in full; 397–553 only by grep and targeted reads of §10 and §13), `docs/lessons.md` (in full), `docs/design.md` (trust boundary 219–266; remote status 3107–3170; Open questions 3672), and the code listed below.
6	
7	## 0. Short version
8	
9	- The remote port is an authenticated JSON API and nothing else. `serve_remote` answers every path outside `/api/v1/` with 404 (`src/app.rs:3023-3026`). There is no static serving, no HTML, and no non-JSON reply anywhere in the port.
10	- The adapter cannot yet express what a browser needs. `respond()` hard-codes `Content-Type: application/json` and takes no headers (`src/adapters/remote.rs:530-553`). `RemoteReply` has no content type or header list (`:389-393`). `read_request` keeps only `Authorization`, `Upgrade` and `Sec-WebSocket-Key`; it drops `Cookie`, `Origin`, `Host` and `User-Agent` (`:444-511`). `respond_upgrade` writes no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (`:519-527`).
11	- The token is bearer-only today, which is why CSRF does not arise. A cookie-carried token makes every `POST` under `control` (send, resume, trust, draft, dictation, ticket decide/resume/close, new session) ambient to any browser that holds it. That changes the threat model and the plan has to answer it (§4 below).
12	- `POST /api/v1/pair` returns the token in its JSON body (`src/app.rs`, `remote_pair`, reply built near line 3650). A browser that wants the token out of script reach must get a different reply shape (a `Set-Cookie` with no token in the body). The issue's sentence "the page's script never sees" depends on that change.
13	- Two claims in the issue's "What exists" are accurate and two are not quite (§6 below). The QR payload has no test anywhere in the tree.
14	
15	## 1. The on-disk record and what rehydrates it, before the pane
16	
17	Nothing a browser does changes any session, project or working-set record. The new state is the device row and a page that holds no state of its own.
18	
19	**On disk**
20	
21	- `identity.json` (in the data directory; `ports::remote::Identity`, `src/ports/remote.rs:26-40`): `server_id`, `server_name`, the DER certificate (base64), `spki_sha256`, `created`, and `listen {lan, port}` (`:57-61`). It is written through the store's atomic path (`src/adapters/remote.rs:43-86`). Its private key is in the Keychain under `remote-key:<server_id>`.
22	- `devices.json`: a bare JSON array of `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96-107`: `id`, `name`, `scope`, `token_sha256`, `created`, `last_seen` with `#[serde(default)]`). It has no version field and is loaded as `Vec<PairedDevice>` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:80-85`). An additive field with a serde default is therefore safe, and the rule that `model.rs` types need a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump does not cover this type. (Confirm the rule's reach: [tree] below.)
23	- The pairing window is **not persisted**. `AppAction::OpenPairing` sets `self.pairing` and emits no effect (`src/core/remote.rs:46-54`). The code, scope and `failures` live in memory. A restart clears the window, the QR and the code.
24	
25	**Rehydration**
26	
27	- Startup loads identity and devices (`src/app.rs` remote section near 2783–2840; `AppAction::IdentityLoaded` in `src/core/remote.rs:23-31`). Devices resume with their token hashes, so a phone whose cookie holds a token keeps working across a host restart. `epoch` changes on every launch, so the page must refetch everything after `hello` (spec §4.4).
28	- A browser device row is created by `/pair` and added through `AppAction::Paired` (`src/core/remote.rs:65-71`, `new_device` at `:163-175`). Its name is `name.trim().chars().take(64)`, taken from the request's `device_name` field, which the client supplies. `remote_pair` defaults it to `"Device"` when empty (`src/app.rs`, `remote_pair`).
29	- Each authenticated request calls `DeviceSeen` (`src/app.rs:3150`). It saves `devices.json` only when `last_seen` moved by 300 s (`src/core/remote.rs:15-18, 72-85`).
30	- Revocation deletes the row and saves (`src/core/remote.rs:86-92`). The next request's `device_by_token` misses, and `authenticate` answers 401 `unauthorized` with "the token is not known; pair again" (`src/app.rs:3127-3150`). A revoked device's socket closes (`tests/remote.rs:2892`, `revoke_closes_the_devices_socket`).
31	- The page itself has no record. Its files are embedded at compile time (the issue's plan; `web/` does not exist yet, `ls` confirms). Nothing rehydrates it; it is served again on every load.
32	- A send is a command through the control port's `serve` and its `operations.log` under the page's op id (`src/app.rs`, `remote_command`, around line 3170ff). Idempotency is the op id, so a page that reloads mid-send has to keep the op somewhere to ask `/ops/{op}` (spec §4.5). Where the page keeps it is an open question.
33	
34	**The pane (what the page shows, and where each part comes from)**
35	
36	- Sessions grouped by project: `GET /api/v1/projects` then `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/sessions` (both routed in `serve_remote`, `src/app.rs:3040-3060`). Each `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637-690`) carries `waiting: bool` (`:657`), `waiting_reason` (`:658`), `kind`, `name`, `liveness`, `card: String` (`:646`), `trust_question` (`:662`), `resume_id`, `last_stop_at_ms` (`:650`), `last_activity_ms` (`:656`).
37	- "Waiting ones first and marked": from `waiting` and `waiting_reason`; or `GET /api/v1/waiting`, which is served (`src/app.rs`, `("GET", ["waiting"])`).
38	- "The one-line excerpt the card shows": the wire view has `card` (`control/src/lib.rs:646`) and no `last_message` field. The spec (`docs/remote-client.md` §4.3, the paragraph on `session.last_response`) names the excerpt `last_message` from the Stop hook. The name and its source do not match this tree. See [tree] in §8.
39	- Last response or screen: `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/last-response` and `/screen?lines=n` are routed to `remote_content_route` (`src/app.rs:3101-3104` and `:1947-2024`; the content kinds and their `ContentView::LastResponse` mapping are at `:1967`). The conversation page `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation` is routed the same way.
40	- Live refresh: `GET /api/v1/events` (WebSocket). The subscription sends `hello`, then `changed`/`removed`. The page applies replies by `revision` (spec §4.2–§4.4). The host side exists (`src/app.rs`, `remote_subscribe` at 2723; the diff pass at 1584–1620 and `observe` at about 1640).
41	- Reply box: `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` is served (`src/app.rs:3066-3068`) and refuses a non-control device with 403 `scope` (see `remote_command`, which checks `device.scope != Scope::Control`, `src/app.rs:3166`). The page would hide the box from the scope, but nothing returns the caller's scope to the caller (§4 F-scope below).
42	- Redaction: every text the page renders goes through the same `redact`/`remote_reply` path as the headset (`src/app.rs`, `remote_reply` at 3695), so the page inherits the existing masking and its bounds (`STRING_CAP`, `NOTES_CAP_ALONE`). Nothing the page adds needs its own policy, as long as the page renders only these bodies.
43	
44	## 2. Code map (as in this worktree)
45	
46	Adapter, `src/adapters/remote.rs`:
47	- `RemoteRequest` 360–373 (`method`, `path`, `query`, `body`, `bearer`, `upgrade`). No cookie, origin, host or user-agent field.
48	- `RemoteReply` 389–393 (`status`, `body`, `authenticated`). No content type, no headers.
49	- `read_request` 444–511. Bearer 487–489; upgrade 491–493; path/query split 495–.
50	- `respond_upgrade` 519–527 (101 with `Upgrade`, `Connection`, `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` only).
51	- `respond` 530–553 (always `application/json`, `Connection: keep-alive`, one write).
52	- `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED = 4`, `MAX_PAIRED = 12` 567–568; `HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` 5 s 570; `IDLE_TIMEOUT` 30 s 573; `PAIR_PER_MINUTE = 6`, `INFO_PER_MINUTE = 60` 583–584; `PAIR_PATH`, `INFO_PATH` 586–587.
53	- `Limits::limited` 631–640: only `/pair` and `/info` have windows; every other path returns "not limited" (so a static path is never rate-limited, only pooled).
54	- Accept loop: a connection past the unauthenticated pool is dropped at accept (`drop(stream)`, line 704). The pool is incremented per accepted connection and only moved to "paired" on the first authenticated reply (`connection`, 770–880; the move is at about 822–834).
55	- `ANSWER_TIMEOUT` 60 s 577; `DRAIN_PER_PASS = 8` 580.
56	- `make_identity` 95–129: `CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())`, so **no subject alternative names**. Validity is rcgen's default, which the doc comment (90–93) gives as "the year 4096". CN is `Switchboard <uuid>`.
57	- `tls_config` 144–158: `ring`, TLS 1.2 and 1.3, no client auth, no ALPN.
58	- `RemotePort::bind` 667–: `0.0.0.0` when `listen.lan`, otherwise `127.0.0.1` (the choice is in `src/app.rs`, `bind_remote`, about 2966–2972).
59	- Pinning helpers `pinned_client`/`Pin` 168–245 (for Rust clients and tests only; a browser has no such hook).
60	- `local_address()` 962–970: the routing address, which is returned even when `lan` is off.
61	
62	Ports, `src/ports/remote.rs`: `Identity` 26–40, `Listen` 57–69 (default port 43187), `Scope` 76–88, `PairedDevice` 96–107.
63	
64	App, `src/app.rs`:
65	- Drain: `serve_pending` pulls up to 8 remote requests per pass (1584–1596), then frames (1598–1606), then the diff/observe path.
66	- `serve_remote` 3017–3125: the `/api/v1/` strip at 3023 (non-matching → 404 `not_found`), `("GET", ["info"])` and `("POST", ["pair"])` answered before authentication (3028–3029), `authenticate` at 3031, `events` upgrade at 3035–3037, the routing match 3040–3110, `hide_workers` on every listing unless `scope=all`.
67	- `authenticate` 3127–3152: a missing bearer and an unknown bearer both answer 401 `unauthorized`, with two different messages (3132, 3145). No record of revoked tokens exists to tell them apart.
68	- `remote_command` 3159ff: checks `device.scope != Scope::Control` (403 `scope`, at 3166), then the op log and `serve`.
69	- `remote_info` 3568–3603: `capabilities` at 3580 (`read`, `control`, `draft`, `scope`, `tickets`, `evidence`, `create`); `pairing_open` 3600. There is no `web` capability and no device-identity endpoint.
70	- `remote_pair` 3606–3666: the body must be JSON (3615); the key check comes **before** the code check (`spki_sha256` mismatch → `PairingFailed` → 403 `wrong_key`, 3636–3645); a wrong code → `PairingFailed` → 403 `wrong_code` (3646–3650); `device_name` defaults to `"Device"`; the reply JSON is `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}` (3659–3665), so **the token is in the body**.
71	- `refuse` 3754–3772 logs `method` and `request.path` (no query string) and the code.
72	- `remote_info`'s `limits` (3585–3599) is what the page would read for its own bounds.
73	- Bind: `bind_remote` 2936–2990.
74	
75	UI, `src/ui/remote.rs`:
76	- Dialog text: the redaction sentence at 71–72 is the only one about what a device sees; nothing about certificate trust.
77	- Pairing window: open with a scope at 213–226 (`OpenPairing` with `pairing_code()` and `draft.scope`).
78	- QR payload built inline at 160–166: `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`, with `addresses` holding one entry, `local_address()` plus the port (157–159). The text form is "Copy invite" at 199–206, which copies the same JSON.
79	- The address line is shown at 188–190 whether or not the listener is on the LAN.
80	- `qr_texture` 280–299 (the `qrcode` crate, 4 px per module, 4-module quiet zone).
81	- The payload construction is **logic inside `ui/`**. CLAUDE.md says logic in `ui/` moves to the core, and there is no test for it (grep of `tests/remote.rs` for `qr`, `invite` and `addresses` finds nothing).
82	
83	Core, `src/core/remote.rs`:
84	- `OpenPairing` 46–54 (code uppercased; `until = now.mono + PAIRING_WINDOW`), `ClosePairing` 55, `PairingFailed` 56–64 (three closes), `Paired` 65–71 (window closes on first success), `DeviceSeen` 72–85, `RevokeDevice` 86–92, `SetDeviceScope` 93–100.
85	- `pairing_at` 149–154; `device_by_token` 143–147 (matches on the token hash); `new_device` 163–175.
86	
87	Swift, `client/`:
88	- `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift`: `ServerInfo` 4–39 (`capabilities`, `pairing_open`, `version`); `PairRequest` 47–64; `PairReply` 66–77 (token, scope, server_id, device_id); `KeyFingerprint.short` 82–89; **`PairingInvite` 94–117, which decodes JSON only** (`parse` at 114–116 uses `Wire.decode`).
89	- `client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift`: `pair` with one argument parses the invite JSON (107–111); with three arguments (`host:port code spki`) it probes `/info` unpinned and builds an invite (112–124); usage text at 10–18.
90	- `client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:103–107` (dev aid, `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` split by newline and parsed) and `:849`/`:883` (the headset's paste field "Paste the QR code's text" and `PairingInvite.parse`).
91	- `client/Apps/SwitchboardVision/SwitchboardVisionApp.swift:56`: the environment variable's doc comment says the value is invites' JSON.
92	- `client/Sources/SwitchboardClientCore/ConnectionManager.swift:474–487`: builds an invite and pairs with `addresses.compactMap(Address.init).first`.
93	
94	Tests, `tests/remote.rs`:
95	- `http` 245–297: a raw TLS client that reads the status line and `Content-Length` only, and returns the body as a `String`. It does not return headers.
96	- `call` 299–325 parses the body as JSON (`serde_json::from_str`, line 322), so a static HTML body would panic it. A new helper is needed for the page.
97	- `get` 327–330.
98	- `info_is_served_to_anyone_and_every_other_read_is_refused_unpaired` 426–475, which asserts `GET /other` → 404 `not_found` (about line 455). This still holds if `/` alone is added.
99	- `the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect` 682–724.
100	- `a_wrong_pin_fails_at_the_handshake_before_any_request` 1395–1404.
101	- `pair_is_rate_limited_per_listener` 1406–1420: asserts six 403 then 429, and `/info` still 200.
102	- `revoke_closes_the_devices_socket` 2892.
103	- `stalled_strangers_fill_their_own_pool_and_never_a_paired_clients` 3226 (the pool test).
104	- Fixtures 1579–1700 (`write_fixtures`), decode check 1829–.

106	
107	Docs:
108	- `docs/remote-client.md`: §4.1 bounds 124–131 (the 4-unauthenticated pool at 125; `/pair` 6/min and `/info` 60/min at 126); §4.2 caps 147–153; §4.3 endpoint table 157–192; line 194 "v1 remote is the table above and nothing more"; §4.4 events 221–268; §5 pairing 302–319 (306 "Require pairing before anything but /info and /pair"; 309 QR and key-before-code; 312 "never in a URL"; 313 `devices.json`; 315 key rotation; 316 revocation); §11 table near 480 (revocation and rotation behaviour).
109	- `docs/design.md`: trust boundary 219–266 (251 "as redacted text on the remote port"); "Remote client (2026-10-12)" 3107–3170 (3157 "Remote devices dialog"); remote status continues to about 3260; Open questions 3672–3678.
110	- `README.md` (Layout table, dev aids, data directory) and `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased) were not opened; CLAUDE.md requires both to change with a user-visible feature.
111	
112	## 3. Findings the plan has to reckon with
113	
114	F1. **No static serving, no headers, no content type in the adapter.** `respond()` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:530-553`) and `RemoteReply` (`:389-393`) have no way to say `text/html`, a `Content-Security-Policy`, `Cache-Control`, or `Set-Cookie`. Every one of the issue's static-path requirements needs an adapter change. The change is small, but it touches the one function every reply goes through.
115	
116	F2. **`read_request` drops every header the browser plan needs.** `Cookie` (cookie option), `Origin` (CSRF on POST and the WebSocket upgrade), `Host` (rebinding), `User-Agent` (device name), `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (subprotocol option). Only `authorization`, `upgrade`, `sec-websocket-key`, `content-length` are read (`:486-493`). Adding them is additive to `RemoteRequest`, which is `pub` and built only in `read_request` and tests (`tests/remote.rs` builds requests through the real socket, so no literal construction needs changing).
117	
118	F3. **`respond_upgrade` omits `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`** (`src/adapters/remote.rs:519-527`). If the page offers a subprotocol carrying the token, the handshake must echo one it accepts. Whether a browser fails the handshake without the echo is a [source] question (§7); the tree sends none.
119	
120	F4. **The token is in the `/pair` reply body** (`src/app.rs`, `remote_pair`, the reply object `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}`, `"token": token` at line 3661). Any `fetch` in the page can read that body. The issue's "the page's script never sees [the token]" needs a browser-specific reply that sets the cookie and omits the token, or the claim does not hold for the pairing response itself.
121	
122	F5. **Cookie-carried auth makes `control` POSTs ambient.** Today the only credential is an `Authorization` header, which a browser never attaches on its own, so a cross-site page cannot send a command. A cookie is attached automatically. `SameSite=Strict` is the browser's answer for cross-site requests (a [source] question about IP-address origins; §7), and an `Origin` check in the adapter or `serve_remote` is the second layer. Neither exists. The `control` endpoints the plan would expose include `send`, `resume`, `trust`, `draft` (including `send`), `dictation`, `POST /projects/{id}/sessions` (a new session with a prompt), and ticket `decide`/`resume`/`close`.
123	
124	F6. **Unauthenticated pool and browser fan-out.** The pool is 4 connections (`src/adapters/remote.rs:567`). A connection counts as unauthenticated until its first authenticated reply, and is closed after 30 s idle (`:573`, and the first-request timeout at 5 s). A page needs at least `/` and a script, plus a favicon request (which the browser makes on its own), and a browser may open several connections in parallel. A fifth connection is dropped at accept (`:704`). The spec's CLI-shaped pool was sized for one client, not a browser's parallel loads. Whether the page as specified (inline script forbidden by CSP, so at least one separate script file) fits in four is a [run] question (§7).
125	
126	F7. **A static path is pooled but never rate-limited.** `Limits::limited` answers "not limited" for any path other than `/pair` and `/info` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:631-640`). The page's own requests count only against the pool. That is the answer the issue asks for under item 4, but it means a stranger's unauthenticated `GET /` costs a pool slot and a frame pass (if served on the frame) with no rate window. Whether to serve static files on the connection thread or the frame is a choice the plan has to make. Both are possible: the page's bytes are constants, and `RemoteIncoming` already carries the channel.
127	
128	F8. **Revocation and "never paired" look the same to the host.** `authenticate` returns 401 `unauthorized` with two different messages for a missing token and an unknown token (`src/app.rs:3127-3150`). Revoked tokens are deleted, not tombstoned (`src/core/remote.rs:86-92`). So the host cannot say "revoked" as opposed to "not paired". The issue's acceptance ("the page says so on its next request") needs either a tombstone (new state, retained hashes) or a page that says "not paired or revoked" for any 401. This is a plan decision, not a settled fact.
129

233	# Issue #230 facts: a web control surface on the remote port
234	
235	Worktree: `/Users/sbgragent/.dispatch/worktrees/340ccb28`, base `7fe8949`. Investigation read: `notes.md`. Nothing was built, run or committed; `git status` is empty. No spike was run (see Unresolved, last item). Browser behaviour could not be tested here: no Chrome or Chromium is installed, and Safari needs a person's hands and a device.
236	
237	## Settled
238	
239	- The remote port answers only `/info` and `/pair` before authentication; every other path is refused unless it is under `/api/v1/`. Evidence: `src/app.rs:3026-3029` (`strip_prefix` and the `("GET", ["info"])` / `("POST", ["pair"])` arms before `authenticate`); notes §0 for the 404.
240	- The host certificate has no subjectAltName. Evidence: `src/adapters/remote.rs:97` (`CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())`).
241	- The host certificate's validity is rcgen's default, `not_after` = year 4096. Evidence: `rcgen-0.14.10/src/certificate.rs:83-85` (registry copy, version pinned in `Cargo.lock`); the tree's own comment at `src/adapters/remote.rs:91-92` says the same.
242	- The host key is P-256 and `spki_sha256` is the hash of the key's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, not of the certificate. Evidence: `src/adapters/remote.rs:91` (doc), `:107-108` (`sha256_hex(&key.subject_public_key_info())`). Consequence: re-issuing the certificate over the same key (new SAN, shorter validity) leaves `spki_sha256` and the QR's `key` unchanged. The key lives in the Keychain and the certificate in `identity.json`; re-issue would need new code to write the new certificate.
243	- Apple's stated requirements for TLS server certificates: validity of 825 days or fewer, a DNS name in the Subject Alternative Name extension, RSA keys of at least 2048 bits, and the rules apply to certificates issued after 1 July 2019. Evidence: https://support.apple.com/103769 (fetched). The same page does not say whether they apply to a certificate the user has accepted as an exception. See Unresolved.
244	- Chrome's 398-day rule is named in the Chromium commit "Enforce 398-day validity for certificates issued on-or-after 2020-09-01" (https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/ae4d6809912f8171b23f6aa43c6a4e8e627de784). I read only the commit title from a search result, so it is a lead; see Unresolved.
245	- RFC 6455 §4.1, client rule: if the server's response includes `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` naming a subprotocol the client did not request, the client MUST fail the connection. The rule is triggered only when the header is present; the RFC says nothing about a response that omits it. Evidence: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455#section-4.1 (fetched).
246	- RFC 6455 §4.1, client request: a browser client MUST send an `Origin` header. Evidence: same section (fetched). The adapter does not read `Origin` (`src/adapters/remote.rs`, `read_request`, per notes F2; keys read are `authorization`, `upgrade`, `sec-websocket-key`, `content-length`).
247	- A token carried in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` would be visible to the page's script. `new WebSocket(url, protocols)` takes the protocol list from script, and the negotiated value is readable from `WebSocket.protocol`. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket/WebSocket (fetched). This rules the subprotocol option out for the "script never sees the token" claim.
248	- Fragments are not sent to the server: the fragment is not part of the `http`/`https` scheme syntax and does not appear in their ABNF. Evidence: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-4.2.5 (fetched). Consequence: a code carried after `#` never reaches the host; a code after `?` is in the request line of `GET /`.
249	- The default `Referrer-Policy` is `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, which sends the path and query string in `Referer` on same-origin requests; `no-referrer` sends no `Referer`. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Referrer-Policy (fetched). Consequence: the page's script and stylesheet requests, made while the HTML is parsed (before any `replaceState`), carry `?code=` in `Referer` unless the page sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
250	- `history.replaceState` changes the URL shown and replaces the current history entry; it does not add an entry. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History/replaceState (fetched). It does not remove the request that already carried the code (the `GET /?code=` and the subresource requests made before the script ran).
251	- The site used for SameSite cookies is the scheme plus the registrable domain; the port is ignored; `http` and `https` are different sites. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/site (search snippet, not fetched in full; treat as settled for host names, see Unresolved for IP addresses).
252	- `maxTouchPoints` is 0 on Mac and typically 5 on phones. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/maxTouchPoints (fetched). The same page does not cover iPad.
253	- `RemoteRequest` is constructed in one place: `src/adapters/remote.rs:506` (`Ok(Some(RemoteRequest {`), defined at `:360`. A grep of `src/` and `tests/` for `RemoteRequest {` finds no other literal. Adding fields is therefore not a breaking change for code in the tree.
254	- `PAIRING_WINDOW` is five minutes and `PAIRING_ATTEMPTS` is 3. Evidence: `src/core/action.rs:972-973`.
255	- `SessionView.card` is a label word, not an excerpt. Evidence: `control/src/lib.rs:645-646` ("The card's word: `CARD_WORKING`, `CARD_IDLE`, 'waiting on you', ..."). The issue's "one-line excerpt the card shows" has no field behind it in the wire view. `control/src/` contains no `last_message`.
256	- `last_message` exists only on the hook event (`src/ports/events.rs:24`, `src/adapters/hooks.rs:71`), not on `SessionView`. Evidence: the grep above.
257	- The schema-version rule in `src/core/model.rs:1-3` is stated for "workspace records" serialized through the model. `devices.json` (`Vec<PairedDevice>`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:80-85`) is not in `model.rs`, so the text does not reach it. Whether to bump anyway is a plan call.
258	- `ServerInfo.capabilities` is `[String]`. Evidence: `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:8`. A new capability string does not change the decoded type.
259	- The `/info` answer is not an authentication of the server. `/info` is answered before authentication (`src/app.rs:3028`), and its `spki_sha256` comes from whichever process holds the socket. A page that compares the URL's `key` with `/info` therefore detects a mismatch of address, not an impostor who answers both. The only binding of the key to the server is TLS, which a browser does not pin to the SPKI. Settled from the tree; the issue's §1 claim should say so.
260	- The QR is built with `qrcode::QrCode::new` (`src/ui/remote.rs:281`), which picks the version and uses error-correction level M by default (`qrcode-0.14.1/src/types.rs:102`). Its doc says it fails only when the data is too long (`qrcode-0.14.1/src/lib.rs:71-74`). A URL of about 150 to 200 bytes is far below the limit; the size was not measured.
261	- The pool of unauthenticated connections is 4, and a fifth is dropped at accept. Spike 22 measured this against its own pinned client: "the pool of 4 was full" and "connection was refused in 0.6 ms" (`spikes/22-remote-port/README.md:79-83`). The spike did not use a browser.

WebKit ITP 2.1 (`https://webkit.org/blog/8613/intelligent-tracking-prevention-2-1/`, search snippet only) caps persistent `document.cookie` cookies at seven days; a later blog says the JS cap was removed in 2022. The two conflict and neither was verified. Needs WebKit release notes or a device.
274	- Whether Safari's `'self'` in `connect-src` allows `wss:` to the same host and port. MDN says `'self'` does not cover WebSocket schemes in every browser. WebKit bug 201591 (`https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=201591`) reports Safari still blocking same-host `wss` as of a February 2021 comment. Current status not checked. A plan that lists `wss://<host>:<port>` explicitly in `connect-src` does not depend on the answer; that recommendation is the plan's to make.
275	- Whether browsers request `/favicon.ico` by themselves and what they do with a 404. Tried: a search. Mozilla bug 1745680 (search snippet) says Firefox, Chrome and Safari request the root path. Current Safari behaviour not checked. A `<link rel="icon">` with a data URI would avoid the request but needs `img-src data:` in the CSP; not tested.
276	- The iPad's user agent in desktop-site mode, and whether `maxTouchPoints > 1` tells an iPad from a Mac. The MDN value is documented for Mac (0) and phones (typically 5); iPad not stated. Needs a device.
277	- Browser limit on concurrent connections to one host. Tried: a search. Secondary sources say 6 for Chrome on HTTP/1.1; RFC 9112 §9.4 (not fetched) says a client SHOULD NOT keep more than 2. The number that matters is how many unauthenticated connections Safari opens for `/`, a script, a stylesheet, a favicon, and the WebSocket on a cold load. Needs a device or a network trace.
278	- Whether a browser allows the host's certificate exception to cover `wss://` on the same host and port in Safari and Chrome for Android. Not found. Needs a device.
279	- Whether `Host`-header rebinding from another origin reaches the host under a certificate exception. Not searched; the cookie argument above depends on the SameSite answer.
280	- Whether the Keychain-stored key and the certificate in `identity.json` can be re-issued with a SAN and a 825-day validity without changing `spki_sha256` (see Settled). The arithmetic holds; no code in the tree does it.
281	- No spike was run. The only browser-behaviour questions are the ones above, and none can be answered on this machine without a browser window driven by hand. A non-browser spike (for example an `openssl` check of the certificate's extensions) would repeat what `src/adapters/remote.rs:97` and `rcgen` already show, so it was not run.
282	
283	## For the owner
284	
285	1. Certificate trust step (issue §1). If Safari and Chrome show a click-through for the current certificate, the plan can keep the click-through as the trust step and say so in the paired-devices dialog. If either browser refuses with no exception (no SAN, 4096-year validity), the plan must re-issue the certificate with an IP SAN and a validity within 825 days (the key and `spki_sha256` stay the same, see Settled), or the browser path does not work at all. Both answers need one phone test with the current build.
286	2. Token transport (issue §2). If cookies are stored and sent on `fetch` and the WebSocket handshake after a click-through (Unresolved), use an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie and a `/pair` reply with no token in the body for browsers, and add `Origin` checking, since a cookie makes `control` POSTs ambient. If cookies are not sent on the WebSocket, the plan must pick another carrier; the subprotocol option is out because script sees it (Settled).
287	3. Code in the URL. The issue puts the code in `?code=`. If the owner accepts that the code reaches the host in the request line, keep it; the plan then needs `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on the page (Settled). If not, the code can go after `#`, which never reaches the host or any `Referer` (Settled), and the page reads `location.hash` before `replaceState`.
288	4. One QR or two (issue §3). The URL replaces the JSON for the headset's paste and `PairingInvite.parse`, which need a Swift URL parser and tests (notes F14). The CLI's three-argument form already needs no JSON. If the owner wants the JSON kept, it stays for the headset and CLI only.
289	5. Identity-change detection (issue §1, notes F19). The page's stored key is readable by any script on the origin if it sits in `localStorage`; a cookie is not. The `/info` key check is an address check, not a server check (Settled), so the owner should decide whether it is worth storing at all.
290	6. Revoked versus never paired (notes F8, acceptance criterion). Today the host cannot tell them apart. A tombstone for revoked token hashes is new state in `devices.json`; the alternative is a page that says "not paired or revoked" for any 401, which does not meet the acceptance wording.
291	7. Caller's scope (notes F9). No endpoint returns it. Owner: a new read endpoint amends §4.3's "nothing more" rule, or the page learns scope by attempting a send.
292	8. Frame or connection thread for the page (notes F7). The page's bytes are constant; serving them on the connection thread avoids a frame pass but is unlimited by rate window, and the pool is the only bound (notes F7). Owner's choice.
293	9. Connections for a cold page load (Unresolved). If a phone's Safari opens more than four unauthenticated connections, the fifth is dropped at accept (spike 22). Needs one device run with the pool counted; the plan may need a larger unauthenticated pool for static paths.
294	10. Acceptance run. Needs a phone on the same network, a real Safari, and a bundle signed with the stable identity (CLAUDE.md, "Platform-specific code"). This is the owner's, not runnable here.
295	11. Shipping items (CLAUDE.md "Adding a feature" steps 4–5): a CHANGELOG line under Unreleased, a README Layout row for `web/`, the design.md remote status section, and the amendment to `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1, §4.3 and §5.
296

# Issue #230: a web control surface on the remote port. Investigation notes

Worktree: `/Users/sbgragent/.dispatch/worktrees/340ccb28`, branch `dispatch/230-a-web-control-surface-the-remote-port-se`, base `7fe8949` (Release 0.4.1). Read-only investigation: no code, tests or builds were run, and no browser was used.

Sources read: `CLAUDE.md` (given in context), `docs/remote-client.md` (lines 1–396 in full; 397–553 only by grep and targeted reads of §10 and §13), `docs/lessons.md` (in full), `docs/design.md` (trust boundary 219–266; remote status 3107–3170; Open questions 3672), and the code listed below.

## 0. Short version

- The remote port is an authenticated JSON API and nothing else. `serve_remote` answers every path outside `/api/v1/` with 404 (`src/app.rs:3023-3026`). There is no static serving, no HTML, and no non-JSON reply anywhere in the port.
- The adapter cannot yet express what a browser needs. `respond()` hard-codes `Content-Type: application/json` and takes no headers (`src/adapters/remote.rs:530-553`). `RemoteReply` has no content type or header list (`:389-393`). `read_request` keeps only `Authorization`, `Upgrade` and `Sec-WebSocket-Key`; it drops `Cookie`, `Origin`, `Host` and `User-Agent` (`:444-511`). `respond_upgrade` writes no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (`:519-527`).
- The token is bearer-only today, which is why CSRF does not arise. A cookie-carried token makes every `POST` under `control` (send, resume, trust, draft, dictation, ticket decide/resume/close, new session) ambient to any browser that holds it. That changes the threat model and the plan has to answer it (§4 below).
- `POST /api/v1/pair` returns the token in its JSON body (`src/app.rs`, `remote_pair`, reply built near line 3650). A browser that wants the token out of script reach must get a different reply shape (a `Set-Cookie` with no token in the body). The issue's sentence "the page's script never sees" depends on that change.
- Two claims in the issue's "What exists" are accurate and two are not quite (§6 below). The QR payload has no test anywhere in the tree.

## 1. The on-disk record and what rehydrates it, before the pane

Nothing a browser does changes any session, project or working-set record. The new state is the device row and a page that holds no state of its own.

**On disk**

- `identity.json` (in the data directory; `ports::remote::Identity`, `src/ports/remote.rs:26-40`): `server_id`, `server_name`, the DER certificate (base64), `spki_sha256`, `created`, and `listen {lan, port}` (`:57-61`). It is written through the store's atomic path (`src/adapters/remote.rs:43-86`). Its private key is in the Keychain under `remote-key:<server_id>`.
- `devices.json`: a bare JSON array of `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96-107`: `id`, `name`, `scope`, `token_sha256`, `created`, `last_seen` with `#[serde(default)]`). It has no version field and is loaded as `Vec<PairedDevice>` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:80-85`). An additive field with a serde default is therefore safe, and the rule that `model.rs` types need a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump does not cover this type. (Confirm the rule's reach: [tree] below.)
- The pairing window is **not persisted**. `AppAction::OpenPairing` sets `self.pairing` and emits no effect (`src/core/remote.rs:46-54`). The code, scope and `failures` live in memory. A restart clears the window, the QR and the code.

**Rehydration**

- Startup loads identity and devices (`src/app.rs` remote section near 2783–2840; `AppAction::IdentityLoaded` in `src/core/remote.rs:23-31`). Devices resume with their token hashes, so a phone whose cookie holds a token keeps working across a host restart. `epoch` changes on every launch, so the page must refetch everything after `hello` (spec §4.4).
- A browser device row is created by `/pair` and added through `AppAction::Paired` (`src/core/remote.rs:65-71`, `new_device` at `:163-175`). Its name is `name.trim().chars().take(64)`, taken from the request's `device_name` field, which the client supplies. `remote_pair` defaults it to `"Device"` when empty (`src/app.rs`, `remote_pair`).
- Each authenticated request calls `DeviceSeen` (`src/app.rs:3150`). It saves `devices.json` only when `last_seen` moved by 300 s (`src/core/remote.rs:15-18, 72-85`).
- Revocation deletes the row and saves (`src/core/remote.rs:86-92`). The next request's `device_by_token` misses, and `authenticate` answers 401 `unauthorized` with "the token is not known; pair again" (`src/app.rs:3127-3150`). A revoked device's socket closes (`tests/remote.rs:2892`, `revoke_closes_the_devices_socket`).
- The page itself has no record. Its files are embedded at compile time (the issue's plan; `web/` does not exist yet, `ls` confirms). Nothing rehydrates it; it is served again on every load.
- A send is a command through the control port's `serve` and its `operations.log` under the page's op id (`src/app.rs`, `remote_command`, around line 3170ff). Idempotency is the op id, so a page that reloads mid-send has to keep the op somewhere to ask `/ops/{op}` (spec §4.5). Where the page keeps it is an open question.

**The pane (what the page shows, and where each part comes from)**

- Sessions grouped by project: `GET /api/v1/projects` then `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/sessions` (both routed in `serve_remote`, `src/app.rs:3040-3060`). Each `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637-690`) carries `waiting: bool` (`:657`), `waiting_reason` (`:658`), `kind`, `name`, `liveness`, `card: String` (`:646`), `trust_question` (`:662`), `resume_id`, `last_stop_at_ms` (`:650`), `last_activity_ms` (`:656`).
- "Waiting ones first and marked": from `waiting` and `waiting_reason`; or `GET /api/v1/waiting`, which is served (`src/app.rs`, `("GET", ["waiting"])`).
- "The one-line excerpt the card shows": the wire view has `card` (`control/src/lib.rs:646`) and no `last_message` field. The spec (`docs/remote-client.md` §4.3, the paragraph on `session.last_response`) names the excerpt `last_message` from the Stop hook. The name and its source do not match this tree. See [tree] in §8.
- Last response or screen: `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/last-response` and `/screen?lines=n` are routed to `remote_content_route` (`src/app.rs:3101-3104` and `:1947-2024`; the content kinds and their `ContentView::LastResponse` mapping are at `:1967`). The conversation page `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation` is routed the same way.
- Live refresh: `GET /api/v1/events` (WebSocket). The subscription sends `hello`, then `changed`/`removed`. The page applies replies by `revision` (spec §4.2–§4.4). The host side exists (`src/app.rs`, `remote_subscribe` at 2723; the diff pass at 1584–1620 and `observe` at about 1640).
- Reply box: `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` is served (`src/app.rs:3066-3068`) and refuses a non-control device with 403 `scope` (see `remote_command`, which checks `device.scope != Scope::Control`, `src/app.rs:3166`). The page would hide the box from the scope, but nothing returns the caller's scope to the caller (§4 F-scope below).
- Redaction: every text the page renders goes through the same `redact`/`remote_reply` path as the headset (`src/app.rs`, `remote_reply` at 3695), so the page inherits the existing masking and its bounds (`STRING_CAP`, `NOTES_CAP_ALONE`). Nothing the page adds needs its own policy, as long as the page renders only these bodies.

## 2. Code map (as in this worktree)

Adapter, `src/adapters/remote.rs`:
- `RemoteRequest` 360–373 (`method`, `path`, `query`, `body`, `bearer`, `upgrade`). No cookie, origin, host or user-agent field.
- `RemoteReply` 389–393 (`status`, `body`, `authenticated`). No content type, no headers.
- `read_request` 444–511. Bearer 487–489; upgrade 491–493; path/query split 495–.
- `respond_upgrade` 519–527 (101 with `Upgrade`, `Connection`, `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` only).
- `respond` 530–553 (always `application/json`, `Connection: keep-alive`, one write).
- `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED = 4`, `MAX_PAIRED = 12` 567–568; `HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` 5 s 570; `IDLE_TIMEOUT` 30 s 573; `PAIR_PER_MINUTE = 6`, `INFO_PER_MINUTE = 60` 583–584; `PAIR_PATH`, `INFO_PATH` 586–587.
- `Limits::limited` 631–640: only `/pair` and `/info` have windows; every other path returns "not limited" (so a static path is never rate-limited, only pooled).
- Accept loop: a connection past the unauthenticated pool is dropped at accept (`drop(stream)`, line 704). The pool is incremented per accepted connection and only moved to "paired" on the first authenticated reply (`connection`, 770–880; the move is at about 822–834).
- `ANSWER_TIMEOUT` 60 s 577; `DRAIN_PER_PASS = 8` 580.
- `make_identity` 95–129: `CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())`, so **no subject alternative names**. Validity is rcgen's default, which the doc comment (90–93) gives as "the year 4096". CN is `Switchboard <uuid>`.
- `tls_config` 144–158: `ring`, TLS 1.2 and 1.3, no client auth, no ALPN.
- `RemotePort::bind` 667–: `0.0.0.0` when `listen.lan`, otherwise `127.0.0.1` (the choice is in `src/app.rs`, `bind_remote`, about 2966–2972).
- Pinning helpers `pinned_client`/`Pin` 168–245 (for Rust clients and tests only; a browser has no such hook).
- `local_address()` 962–970: the routing address, which is returned even when `lan` is off.

Ports, `src/ports/remote.rs`: `Identity` 26–40, `Listen` 57–69 (default port 43187), `Scope` 76–88, `PairedDevice` 96–107.

App, `src/app.rs`:
- Drain: `serve_pending` pulls up to 8 remote requests per pass (1584–1596), then frames (1598–1606), then the diff/observe path.
- `serve_remote` 3017–3125: the `/api/v1/` strip at 3023 (non-matching → 404 `not_found`), `("GET", ["info"])` and `("POST", ["pair"])` answered before authentication (3028–3029), `authenticate` at 3031, `events` upgrade at 3035–3037, the routing match 3040–3110, `hide_workers` on every listing unless `scope=all`.
- `authenticate` 3127–3152: a missing bearer and an unknown bearer both answer 401 `unauthorized`, with two different messages (3132, 3145). No record of revoked tokens exists to tell them apart.
- `remote_command` 3159ff: checks `device.scope != Scope::Control` (403 `scope`, at 3166), then the op log and `serve`.
- `remote_info` 3568–3603: `capabilities` at 3580 (`read`, `control`, `draft`, `scope`, `tickets`, `evidence`, `create`); `pairing_open` 3600. There is no `web` capability and no device-identity endpoint.
- `remote_pair` 3606–3666: the body must be JSON (3615); the key check comes **before** the code check (`spki_sha256` mismatch → `PairingFailed` → 403 `wrong_key`, 3636–3645); a wrong code → `PairingFailed` → 403 `wrong_code` (3646–3650); `device_name` defaults to `"Device"`; the reply JSON is `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}` (3659–3665), so **the token is in the body**.
- `refuse` 3754–3772 logs `method` and `request.path` (no query string) and the code.
- `remote_info`'s `limits` (3585–3599) is what the page would read for its own bounds.
- Bind: `bind_remote` 2936–2990.

UI, `src/ui/remote.rs`:
- Dialog text: the redaction sentence at 71–72 is the only one about what a device sees; nothing about certificate trust.
- Pairing window: open with a scope at 213–226 (`OpenPairing` with `pairing_code()` and `draft.scope`).
- QR payload built inline at 160–166: `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`, with `addresses` holding one entry, `local_address()` plus the port (157–159). The text form is "Copy invite" at 199–206, which copies the same JSON.
- The address line is shown at 188–190 whether or not the listener is on the LAN.
- `qr_texture` 280–299 (the `qrcode` crate, 4 px per module, 4-module quiet zone).
- The payload construction is **logic inside `ui/`**. CLAUDE.md says logic in `ui/` moves to the core, and there is no test for it (grep of `tests/remote.rs` for `qr`, `invite` and `addresses` finds nothing).

Core, `src/core/remote.rs`:
- `OpenPairing` 46–54 (code uppercased; `until = now.mono + PAIRING_WINDOW`), `ClosePairing` 55, `PairingFailed` 56–64 (three closes), `Paired` 65–71 (window closes on first success), `DeviceSeen` 72–85, `RevokeDevice` 86–92, `SetDeviceScope` 93–100.
- `pairing_at` 149–154; `device_by_token` 143–147 (matches on the token hash); `new_device` 163–175.

Swift, `client/`:
- `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift`: `ServerInfo` 4–39 (`capabilities`, `pairing_open`, `version`); `PairRequest` 47–64; `PairReply` 66–77 (token, scope, server_id, device_id); `KeyFingerprint.short` 82–89; **`PairingInvite` 94–117, which decodes JSON only** (`parse` at 114–116 uses `Wire.decode`).
- `client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift`: `pair` with one argument parses the invite JSON (107–111); with three arguments (`host:port code spki`) it probes `/info` unpinned and builds an invite (112–124); usage text at 10–18.
- `client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:103–107` (dev aid, `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` split by newline and parsed) and `:849`/`:883` (the headset's paste field "Paste the QR code's text" and `PairingInvite.parse`).
- `client/Apps/SwitchboardVision/SwitchboardVisionApp.swift:56`: the environment variable's doc comment says the value is invites' JSON.
- `client/Sources/SwitchboardClientCore/ConnectionManager.swift:474–487`: builds an invite and pairs with `addresses.compactMap(Address.init).first`.

Tests, `tests/remote.rs`:
- `http` 245–297: a raw TLS client that reads the status line and `Content-Length` only, and returns the body as a `String`. It does not return headers.
- `call` 299–325 parses the body as JSON (`serde_json::from_str`, line 322), so a static HTML body would panic it. A new helper is needed for the page.
- `get` 327–330.
- `info_is_served_to_anyone_and_every_other_read_is_refused_unpaired` 426–475, which asserts `GET /other` → 404 `not_found` (about line 455). This still holds if `/` alone is added.
- `the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect` 682–724.
- `a_wrong_pin_fails_at_the_handshake_before_any_request` 1395–1404.
- `pair_is_rate_limited_per_listener` 1406–1420: asserts six 403 then 429, and `/info` still 200.
- `revoke_closes_the_devices_socket` 2892.
- `stalled_strangers_fill_their_own_pool_and_never_a_paired_clients` 3226 (the pool test).
- Fixtures 1579–1700 (`write_fixtures`), decode check 1829–.
- No test of the QR payload.

Docs:
- `docs/remote-client.md`: §4.1 bounds 124–131 (the 4-unauthenticated pool at 125; `/pair` 6/min and `/info` 60/min at 126); §4.2 caps 147–153; §4.3 endpoint table 157–192; line 194 "v1 remote is the table above and nothing more"; §4.4 events 221–268; §5 pairing 302–319 (306 "Require pairing before anything but /info and /pair"; 309 QR and key-before-code; 312 "never in a URL"; 313 `devices.json`; 315 key rotation; 316 revocation); §11 table near 480 (revocation and rotation behaviour).
- `docs/design.md`: trust boundary 219–266 (251 "as redacted text on the remote port"); "Remote client (2026-10-12)" 3107–3170 (3157 "Remote devices dialog"); remote status continues to about 3260; Open questions 3672–3678.
- `README.md` (Layout table, dev aids, data directory) and `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased) were not opened; CLAUDE.md requires both to change with a user-visible feature.

## 3. Findings the plan has to reckon with

F1. **No static serving, no headers, no content type in the adapter.** `respond()` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:530-553`) and `RemoteReply` (`:389-393`) have no way to say `text/html`, a `Content-Security-Policy`, `Cache-Control`, or `Set-Cookie`. Every one of the issue's static-path requirements needs an adapter change. The change is small, but it touches the one function every reply goes through.

F2. **`read_request` drops every header the browser plan needs.** `Cookie` (cookie option), `Origin` (CSRF on POST and the WebSocket upgrade), `Host` (rebinding), `User-Agent` (device name), `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (subprotocol option). Only `authorization`, `upgrade`, `sec-websocket-key`, `content-length` are read (`:486-493`). Adding them is additive to `RemoteRequest`, which is `pub` and built only in `read_request` and tests (`tests/remote.rs` builds requests through the real socket, so no literal construction needs changing).

F3. **`respond_upgrade` omits `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`** (`src/adapters/remote.rs:519-527`). If the page offers a subprotocol carrying the token, the handshake must echo one it accepts. Whether a browser fails the handshake without the echo is a [source] question (§7); the tree sends none.

F4. **The token is in the `/pair` reply body** (`src/app.rs`, `remote_pair`, the reply object `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}`, `"token": token` at line 3661). Any `fetch` in the page can read that body. The issue's "the page's script never sees [the token]" needs a browser-specific reply that sets the cookie and omits the token, or the claim does not hold for the pairing response itself.

F5. **Cookie-carried auth makes `control` POSTs ambient.** Today the only credential is an `Authorization` header, which a browser never attaches on its own, so a cross-site page cannot send a command. A cookie is attached automatically. `SameSite=Strict` is the browser's answer for cross-site requests (a [source] question about IP-address origins; §7), and an `Origin` check in the adapter or `serve_remote` is the second layer. Neither exists. The `control` endpoints the plan would expose include `send`, `resume`, `trust`, `draft` (including `send`), `dictation`, `POST /projects/{id}/sessions` (a new session with a prompt), and ticket `decide`/`resume`/`close`.

F6. **Unauthenticated pool and browser fan-out.** The pool is 4 connections (`src/adapters/remote.rs:567`). A connection counts as unauthenticated until its first authenticated reply, and is closed after 30 s idle (`:573`, and the first-request timeout at 5 s). A page needs at least `/` and a script, plus a favicon request (which the browser makes on its own), and a browser may open several connections in parallel. A fifth connection is dropped at accept (`:704`). The spec's CLI-shaped pool was sized for one client, not a browser's parallel loads. Whether the page as specified (inline script forbidden by CSP, so at least one separate script file) fits in four is a [run] question (§7).

F7. **A static path is pooled but never rate-limited.** `Limits::limited` answers "not limited" for any path other than `/pair` and `/info` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:631-640`). The page's own requests count only against the pool. That is the answer the issue asks for under item 4, but it means a stranger's unauthenticated `GET /` costs a pool slot and a frame pass (if served on the frame) with no rate window. Whether to serve static files on the connection thread or the frame is a choice the plan has to make. Both are possible: the page's bytes are constants, and `RemoteIncoming` already carries the channel.

F8. **Revocation and "never paired" look the same to the host.** `authenticate` returns 401 `unauthorized` with two different messages for a missing token and an unknown token (`src/app.rs:3127-3150`). Revoked tokens are deleted, not tombstoned (`src/core/remote.rs:86-92`). So the host cannot say "revoked" as opposed to "not paired". The issue's acceptance ("the page says so on its next request") needs either a tombstone (new state, retained hashes) or a page that says "not paired or revoked" for any 401. This is a plan decision, not a settled fact.

F9. **The page needs its own scope and nothing returns it.** No endpoint returns the caller's scope; `authenticate` returns the `PairedDevice` but nothing serialises it. `/info` has the capability list, not the caller's scope. The reply box must be hidden from scope, so the page either gets a new read endpoint (§4.3 says "v1 remote is the table above and nothing more", `docs/remote-client.md:194`, so this amends the spec) or learns scope by attempting a send.

F10. **The QR's address and the listener disagree when LAN is off.** With `listen.lan` false the listener is `127.0.0.1` (`src/app.rs`, `bind_remote`), but the pairing window still shows `local_address()` (`src/ui/remote.rs:157-159`), which is the LAN address. A phone scanning it reaches nothing. The URL form would carry the same address. The existing behaviour is not this issue's, but the URL form makes it more visible.

F11. **One address in the QR.** `addresses` holds one entry (`src/ui/remote.rs:164`). The URL form carries one host, so a phone on a different interface has no fallback. The spec's `addresses` array (§5, line 309) is already a single item in practice.

F12. **The certificate has no SAN.** `CertificateParams::new(Vec::new())` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:95-110`) and rcgen's default 4096 validity mean every browser sees a name mismatch as well as a self-signed chain, on the URL's IP host. The click-through is therefore the only trust step, as the issue says, and the exception has to hold for `wss://` on the same origin (a [source] question).

F13. **The QR payload is logic under `ui/` with no test.** Building `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}` happens inside `pairing()` (`src/ui/remote.rs:160-166`). # Issue #230 facts: a web control surface on the remote port

Worktree: `/Users/sbgragent/.dispatch/worktrees/340ccb28`, base `7fe8949`. Investigation read: `notes.md`. Nothing was built, run or committed; `git status` is empty. No spike was run (see Unresolved, last item). Browser behaviour could not be tested here: no Chrome or Chromium is installed, and Safari needs a person's hands and a device.

## Settled

- The remote port answers only `/info` and `/pair` before authentication; every other path is refused unless it is under `/api/v1/`. Evidence: `src/app.rs:3026-3029` (`strip_prefix` and the `("GET", ["info"])` / `("POST", ["pair"])` arms before `authenticate`); notes §0 for the 404.
- The host certificate has no subjectAltName. Evidence: `src/adapters/remote.rs:97` (`CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())`).
- The host certificate's validity is rcgen's default, `not_after` = year 4096. Evidence: `rcgen-0.14.10/src/certificate.rs:83-85` (registry copy, version pinned in `Cargo.lock`); the tree's own comment at `src/adapters/remote.rs:91-92` says the same.
- The host key is P-256 and `spki_sha256` is the hash of the key's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, not of the certificate. Evidence: `src/adapters/remote.rs:91` (doc), `:107-108` (`sha256_hex(&key.subject_public_key_info())`). Consequence: re-issuing the certificate over the same key (new SAN, shorter validity) leaves `spki_sha256` and the QR's `key` unchanged. The key lives in the Keychain and the certificate in `identity.json`; re-issue would need new code to write the new certificate.
- Apple's stated requirements for TLS server certificates: validity of 825 days or fewer, a DNS name in the Subject Alternative Name extension, RSA keys of at least 2048 bits, and the rules apply to certificates issued after 1 July 2019. Evidence: https://support.apple.com/103769 (fetched). The same page does not say whether they apply to a certificate the user has accepted as an exception. See Unresolved.
- Chrome's 398-day rule is named in the Chromium commit "Enforce 398-day validity for certificates issued on-or-after 2020-09-01" (https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/ae4d6809912f8171b23f6aa43c6a4e8e627de784). I read only the commit title from a search result, so it is a lead; see Unresolved.
- RFC 6455 §4.1, client rule: if the server's response includes `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` naming a subprotocol the client did not request, the client MUST fail the connection. The rule is triggered only when the header is present; the RFC says nothing about a response that omits it. Evidence: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455#section-4.1 (fetched).
- RFC 6455 §4.1, client request: a browser client MUST send an `Origin` header. Evidence: same section (fetched). The adapter does not read `Origin` (`src/adapters/remote.rs`, `read_request`, per notes F2; keys read are `authorization`, `upgrade`, `sec-websocket-key`, `content-length`).
- A token carried in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` would be visible to the page's script. `new WebSocket(url, protocols)` takes the protocol list from script, and the negotiated value is readable from `WebSocket.protocol`. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket/WebSocket (fetched). This rules the subprotocol option out for the "script never sees the token" claim.
- Fragments are not sent to the server: the fragment is not part of the `http`/`https` scheme syntax and does not appear in their ABNF. Evidence: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-4.2.5 (fetched). Consequence: a code carried after `#` never reaches the host; a code after `?` is in the request line of `GET /`.
- The default `Referrer-Policy` is `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, which sends the path and query string in `Referer` on same-origin requests; `no-referrer` sends no `Referer`. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Referrer-Policy (fetched). Consequence: the page's script and stylesheet requests, made while the HTML is parsed (before any `replaceState`), carry `?code=` in `Referer` unless the page sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
- `history.replaceState` changes the URL shown and replaces the current history entry; it does not add an entry. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History/replaceState (fetched). It does not remove the request that already carried the code (the `GET /?code=` and the subresource requests made before the script ran).
- The site used for SameSite cookies is the scheme plus the registrable domain; the port is ignored; `http` and `https` are different sites. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/site (search snippet, not fetched in full; treat as settled for host names, see Unresolved for IP addresses).
- `maxTouchPoints` is 0 on Mac and typically 5 on phones. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/maxTouchPoints (fetched). The same page does not cover iPad.
- `RemoteRequest` is constructed in one place: `src/adapters/remote.rs:506` (`Ok(Some(RemoteRequest {`), defined at `:360`. A grep of `src/` and `tests/` for `RemoteRequest {` finds no other literal. Adding fields is therefore not a breaking change for code in the tree.
- `PAIRING_WINDOW` is five minutes and `PAIRING_ATTEMPTS` is 3. Evidence: `src/core/action.rs:972-973`.
- `SessionView.card` is a label word, not an excerpt. Evidence: `control/src/lib.rs:645-646` ("The card's word: `CARD_WORKING`, `CARD_IDLE`, 'waiting on you', ..."). The issue's "one-line excerpt the card shows" has no field behind it in the wire view. `control/src/` contains no `last_message`.
- `last_message` exists only on the hook event (`src/ports/events.rs:24`, `src/adapters/hooks.rs:71`), not on `SessionView`. Evidence: the grep above.
- The schema-version rule in `src/core/model.rs:1-3` is stated for "workspace records" serialized through the model. `devices.json` (`Vec<PairedDevice>`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:80-85`) is not in `model.rs`, so the text does not reach it. Whether to bump anyway is a plan call.
- `ServerInfo.capabilities` is `[String]`. Evidence: `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:8`. A new capability string does not change the decoded type.
- The `/info` answer is not an authentication of the server. `/info` is answered before authentication (`src/app.rs:3028`), and its `spki_sha256` comes from whichever process holds the socket. A page that compares the URL's `key` with `/info` therefore detects a mismatch of address, not an impostor who answers both. The only binding of the key to the server is TLS, which a browser does not pin to the SPKI. Settled from the tree; the issue's §1 claim should say so.
- The QR is built with `qrcode::QrCode::new` (`src/ui/remote.rs:281`), which picks the version and uses error-correction level M by default (`qrcode-0.14.1/src/types.rs:102`). Its doc says it fails only when the data is too long (`qrcode-0.14.1/src/lib.rs:71-74`). A URL of about 150 to 200 bytes is far below the limit; the size was not measured.
- The pool of unauthenticated connections is 4, and a fifth is dropped at accept. Spike 22 measured this against its own pinned client: "the pool of 4 was full" and "connection was refused in 0.6 ms" (`spikes/22-remote-port/README.md:79-83`). The spike did not use a browser.
